reason: Non-resupinate means the flower or leaf is not turned upside down. That is the negation of FLOPO:0991166 resupinate, whose bearers already include flower, sporophyll, inflorescence and leaf.

label: palmatifid
definition: A palmately lobed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut palmately into lobes, with the incisions reaching about halfway to the base.
reason: This is the palmate counterpart of FLOPO:0991078 pinnatifid. The floras contrast it with 'partite' ('palmatifid or partite'), so the depth of the cut matters, and FLOPO:0991158 palmately lobed alone would lose it.

label: drupe-like
definition: A structural quality inhering in a fruit or fruit part by virtue of its resembling a drupe: a fleshy or leathery outer layer enclosing one or more hard stones, without being a true drupe.
reason: The floras use it for fruits and false fruits that are not true drupes, so rule:bearer to drupe fruit (PO_0030103) would be wrong. It follows the existing FLOPO resemblance classes cherry-like and raceme-like.

'Flowering stems' and 'flowering branches' describe the state of the part: it bears flowers, unlike a sterile shoot. config/flora_context_words.tsv already maps 'flowering' to the flowering stage (PO_0007616). This is not a quality term.

label: monopodial
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's main axis growing on continuously from its apical bud, with the lateral branches subordinate to it.
reason: This is a standard architecture term for stems, rhizomes and trunks. The note on FLOPO:0991034 indeterminate says monopodial is related to it but not the same, and indeterminate is defined for inflorescences only.
Rotundate (rounded) is used for apices and bases. PATO obtuse has the synonym 'roundish', and config/flora_union_pairs.tsv already maps 'rounded' to PATO_0001935.
This means having erect branches close to and parallel with the main axis, which is FLOPO:0991180 fastigiate. Its bearers already include stem, branch and whole plant.
This negates PATO_0001963 revolute (edges rolled backwards) on leaf margins and similar edges. The French 'bords non enroulés' has the same reading.
This is a relation that needs the region it refers to ('confined to the costa', 'to distal pinnae'). Without that second term it is not a quality, like 'covered' in the previous review.

label: sordid
definition: A color quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being of a dull, dingy, impure hue, usually a greyish or brownish white.
reason: This is a standard colour word for pappus and hairs. PATO_0000328 low saturation (pale) and FLOPO:0991106 dull (reflectivity) do not mean a dirtied off-white.

'Thecae, sori or sepals not confluent' means the like parts stay separate rather than running together. That is FLOPO:0991068 free, as the previous review decided for 'separate'. PATO_0002512 confluent with is relational and is not used here.
French 'déchiré' (torn) on calyx, valves and sheaths means irregularly torn. FLOPO:0991115 lacerate is defined as cut as if torn.

label: sausage-shaped
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cylindrical with rounded ends and often slightly curved, like a sausage.
reason: Neither PATO nor FLOPO has allantoid. PATO_0001873 cylindrical leaves out the rounded ends and the curve that fruits, sori and indusia are described with.
This compound joins two existing values: serrated (PATO_0001206) and scalloped (PATO_0001889, synonym crenate). It is annotated as a continuum between them, like 'linear-lanceolate'.

label: evenly spaced
definition: A positional quality inhering in a set of structures of the same kind by virtue of the distances between neighbouring members being about equal.
reason: This is about the spacing of veins, ribs and pairs along an axis. It sits beside FLOPO:0991189 distant and FLOPO:0991190 approximate and is a quality of a set, like FLOPO:0991102 equal.

label: multistemmed
definition: A branched quality inhering in a whole plant by virtue of the plant's having several main stems arising from at or near ground level instead of a single trunk.
reason: This is a habit word, used only on the whole plant, and it is the opposite of single-trunked. It states no number, so the count pattern does not fit it. FLOPO has no class for it.
On organs ('sepal outside non-glandular') and on hairs ('poils non glandulaires') it means without glands. PO_0005656 has gland as a synonym, matching the previous rule for 'gland'.
This is an ecological adaptation, or a general look ('d'aspect xérophytique'), not a defined morphological quality. The traits behind it (small, thick, hairy leaves) should be annotated directly.
Puckered (and French 'gaufré') means the surface is drawn into many small wrinkles or creases. That matches PATO_0001359 rugose.
This is a variant spelling of lacerate (margin irregularly cut, as if torn). FLOPO:0991115 was added in the previous review.
The shape is cylindrical. 'Narrowly' only says it is slender and gives no measurable ratio, so it is kept with the source words, not made into a separate term.
In the examples (midnerves, vittae, necks, stigmas, lobes) 'not distinct' means not clearly visible or marked off. That is the previous rule for 'indistinct' → PATO_0000464.

label: glumaceous
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being dry, firm-membranous and chaffy, like the glume of a grass.
reason: This is a texture of bracts, sepals and perianths. It is firmer and less translucent than FLOPO:0991047 scarious, and the floras pair it with 'membranous' as a separate value.
The examples mix two senses: bearing vesicles (a part) and bladdery or inflated (PATO_0002376 inflated). Several are fragments ('or vesicles.'). No single term fits.

In PATO, apiculate is only a synonym of the attribute PATO_0000944 sharpness, so there is no apiculate value to negate. A part that is not apiculate does not end in a short abrupt point, which is the negation of FLOPO:0991054 mucronate.
Apricot is a pale yellowish orange.
'Tinted' needs the colour ('tinted pink', 'teinté de pourpre'). The colour is the quality, like 'covered' in the previous review.

Secondary veins looping before the margin are the brochidodromous venation of the leaf, so the rule applies only to leaf and vein bearers. 'Branch looping back' is a different sense and is not covered.
The colour stated is rose-pink as a faint wash. Where the tinge is limited to a region ('at lobe tips'), that region is the part of the bearer in the existing region pattern.
Bivalved means composed of, or opening by, two valves ('composées de deux valves'). It is a count of parts (valve = 2), like '5-nerved', not a quality term.
